headline: Venture Global, a major US exporter of liquefied natural gas, has signed equipment deals for up to 16 large gas power units, most still conditional, to supply AI data centers.
score_reason: Large, concrete deals reported by several outlets, but most purchases are still conditional.
importance_line: People living near US data centers may see more private gas plants built beside them, grid operators could face less pressure from these sites, and the company is betting on customers it has not yet named, so the plan could shrink.
source: OilPrice.com, citing a Venture Global regulatory filing
summary: OilPrice.com reports, in a piece carried by Yahoo Finance, that Venture Global, the US liquefied natural gas (LNG) exporter, signed agreements with GE Vernova and Baker Hughes for up to 16 gas power units of 720 megawatts each, about 11.5 gigawatts in all, backing its aim of up to 10 gigawatts of AI computing capacity by the end of 2034. The plants would run apart from the public grid for data centers on company-controlled land, and a regulatory filing values the equipment deals at about $17.2 billion if every contemplated purchase goes ahead, though most remain conditional and the first purchase order is only expected by the end of 2026.
notes: WSJ exclusive and Reuters carried the story; the WSJ page was blocked; text read on Yahoo Finance (OilPrice copy). Summary rests on a company filing, so it is an announced plan, not built capacity.
